::: {#def-paired-t-test}
#### Paired t-test

Let $(x_{1,1}, x_{1,2}), \ldots, (x_{n,1}, x_{n,2})$
be pairs of related measurements,
such as the same participants measured at two times,
and let $d_i \eqdef x_{i,2} - x_{i,1}$ be the within-pair differences,
with population mean $\mu_d$.
The **paired t-test** of $H_0: \mu_d = 0$ against $H_1: \mu_d \neq 0$
is the one-sample t-test (@def-one-sample-t-test)
of $H_0: \mu = 0$ applied to $\dsn{d}$.
:::
